sources.title: Finite element error analysis of wave equations with dynamic boundary conditions: L² estimates
sources.supported_claim: The abstract variational wave framework includes a positive boundary-mass term and dynamic boundary equation with normal derivative forcing; the prototype assumes positive constant boundary stiffness and coercive time-independent bilinear form.
sources.use_for_hdb: Structural comparison for the bulk-plus-boundary mass norm and boundary force sign.
sources.transfer_limit: The paper's boundary-Laplacian coefficient beta is not the HDB boundary stiffness beta(t): its kappa is the analogous stiffness. HDB W(t,z) and beta(t) may be noncoercive/time dependent. No normal-derivative output certificate or floating-point interval validation is imported.

sources.title: Damped energy-norm a posteriori error estimates for fully discrete approximations of the wave equation using C2-reconstructions with the leapfrog scheme
locators: Section 4, error upper bound; equation (1.7) and Remark 4.5
sources.supported_claim: The work provides reliable reconstructed-residual upper bounds for a damped time-integrated bulk energy norm for a Dirichlet scalar wave discretized by continuous finite elements and leapfrog; the displayed asymptotic leading estimate has explicit correction/higher-order terms that cannot be discarded in certification.
sources.use_for_hdb: Motivates evaluating the continuous residual of a smooth reconstruction, separately from checking discrete equations or grid convergence.
sources.transfer_limit: Its Dirichlet, zero-initial-data/source regularity and fixed-mesh/time-step framework is not the present dynamic-boundary model. The retrieved text does not establish directed-rounding coefficient/residual enclosures or a pointwise normal-derivative trace bound.

sources.title: A posteriori error estimates and space-adaptive mesh refinements for time-dependent scattering problems
sources.supported_claim: Residual-based a posteriori bounds are derived for boundary integral/convolution-quadrature discretizations of exterior acoustic Dirichlet scattering. Theorem 1 retains a temporal error term and a constant depending on geometry, final time and data regularity.
sources.use_for_hdb: Illustrates the distinction between a proved reliable residual estimator and a fully explicit end-to-end numerical enclosure.
sources.transfer_limit: Exterior Dirichlet scattering and boundary integral density are different from a finite collar, boundary mass and shell normal derivative. Its unspecified constant C and time remainder are not numerical HDB error bars.

sources.title: An adaptive integrating factor midpoint method for second order evolution equations
sources.supported_claim: The abstract reports residual energy estimates and a quadratic continuous time reconstruction for integrating-factor midpoint approximations of wave-type equations.
sources.use_for_hdb: Recent candidate for later method selection.
sources.transfer_limit: The body was not read. No claim about dynamic boundary applicability, rigorous floating-point implementation or derivative observations is made.

sources.title: Finite element exponential integration for rough solutions of nonlinear wave equations. Part II: Dynamic boundary conditions on curved domains
sources.supported_claim: The abstract reports fully discrete low-regularity convergence in a weak displacement-velocity norm for nonlinear wave equations with dynamic boundary conditions on curved domains.
sources.use_for_hdb: Recent structural neighbor for bulk-surface geometry and weak norms.
sources.transfer_limit: Convergence in weak norms is not an a posteriori interval enclosure or a bound on the normal derivative. The body was not read.

synthesis_claim: The bounded search found useful structural and reconstruction methods, but no directly transferable fully explicit interval certificate for the present time-dependent boundary-mass equation and normal-derivative shell output. This is not a novelty or nonexistence claim.
